Project Description: There is proposal for concrete lining of Khanna distributary from RD 72990 to 126900 providing cup shaped section of cement concrete having thickness of 60 mm and side slope of 1:1. The project estimate of Khanna distributary is sanctioned vide file no. WR 6790-2/CANALS dated 15/07/2022 by Government of Punjab. Currently, Khanna distributary is unlined having trapezoidal section. Due to its unlined section, there is heavy growth of weeds in the inner section of distributary which requires lots of maintenance, causes obstruction to the flow of water and hence make it difficult to run distributary at its design discharge capacity. In peak paddy season, it becomes difficult to make sufficient water available to tail end farmers. Due to its unlined section, there is always a possibility of breach of distributary during peak paddy season. Considering as explained above, concrete lining of Khanna distributary is proposed in order to provide irrigation water to the farmers as per design.

Project Description:
River Ravi originates from the Himalayas in the Chamba district of
Himachal Pradesh near the Rohtang Pass and enters in Punjab plains near Madhopur
carrying a lot of silt & minor gravel with it. In the previous years whenever Ravi river
was at its peak, it deposited lot of silt in the plain areas of Punjab because here the
river water eventually slows down. This year on dates 14, 24 & 27 of August 2025 due
to heavy rainfall in the uphill region floods caused heavy damages to Dhussi Bandh,
Nearby villages and cultivable lands. On u/s side the taming of river with the
embankments have restricted the flow of river within the embankments but it has also
reduced the water carrying capacity of river as the deposition of silt is also restricted
within embankments. The river has not been cleaned of silt and other deposits from a
long time. The reduced water carrying capacity is the main reason behind the severity
of floods which have occurred in the last few years.

Project Description:
River Ravi originates from the Himalayas in the Chamba district of Himachal Pradesh near the Rohtang Pass and enters in Punjab plains near Madhopur carrying a lot of silt & minor gravel with it. In the previous year's whenever Ravi River was at its peak, it deposited lot of silt in the plain areas of Punjab because here the river water eventually slows down. This year on dates 14, 24 & 27 of August 2025 due to heavy rainfall in the uphill region floods caused heavy damages to Dhussi Bandh, Nearby villages and cultivable lands. On u/s side the taming of river with the embankments have restricted the flow of river within the embankments but it has also reduced the water carrying capacity of river as the deposition of silt is also restricted 
within embankments. The river has not been cleaned of silt and other deposits from a long time. The reduced water carrying capacity is the main reason behind the severity of floods which have occurred in the last few years.

Project Description: The villages of Swamipur , Kherbag , Bhabhour Sahib etc. are situated on the Upstream  of the Nangal Dam Reservior . This area lies in Nangal, at the foothills of the Shiwalik Hills adjoining Himachal Pradesh. The entire area is sub mountainous, situated at a high altitude, and no irrigation facilities. The agricultural land in most parts of the  area is devoid of irrigation infrastructure and depends solely on rainfall. The land in this region is located at a higher elevation than the nearest sources of water supply for irrigation. Therefore, flow irrigation is not feasible. Under this proposal, irrigation water will be provided to the villages  through a lift irrigation scheme. This scheme involves lifting water from the Nangal Dam Reservior using pumping sets and transferring it to delivery tanks strategically located for redistribution under gravity flow. The water will then be then be supplied to the fields through different supply lines to cover the entire cultivable area.

Project Description:
The proposed project involves desilting and restoration of existing check dams located at Village Sekhowal Beet, Tehsil Garhshankar, District Hoshiarpur, Punjab, falling under PLPA, 1900 (Sections 4 & 5). The check dams were originally constructed under a World Bank–assisted watershed development project for rainwater harvesting and ecological conservation.

Over time, the check dams have become heavily silted and non-functional, resulting in loss of water storage capacity, reduced groundwater recharge, soil erosion, and degradation of forest vegetation. The proposed activity is limited strictly to desilting and restoration of existing structures, with no expansion, no tree felling, and no change in land use.

The restoration will revive rainwater storage at the foothills, help retain soil moisture in surrounding hill areas beyond the monsoon season, and support forest regeneration, wildlife sustenance, and groundwater recharge. The project is purely environmental conservation-oriented
